Title: Roll 'em Raceway - Super Mario Wiki, the Mario encyclopedia
URL: https://www.mariowiki.com/Roll_%27em_Raceway
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
Roll 'em Raceway is a board that appears in Super Mario Party Jamboree. It takes place on a circuit race course with a pit stop, surrounded by grasslands. Players travel on this board by driving in a race car, as opposed to by foot as in other boards. This board features an exclusive item known as the Turbo Dice, which allows players to roll four Dice Blocks, giving them a range from four to forty spaces to travel in a single turn, at the cost of not being able to interact with any board events (including star exchange). Completing the first lap awards the player 10 coins, completing the second lap awards 20 coins, and the reward is increased by 10 coins for every subsequent lap cleared.
...

The dice items that the player could potentially receive include the Creepy Dice Block, Double Dice, Triple Dice, Custom Dice Block, Payday Double Dice, Payday Triple Dice, or Turbo Dice.
- When the player passes under the arch, they complete a lap and earn bonus coins. Completing the first lap awards the player 10 coins, completing the second lap awards 20 coins, and the reward is increased by 10 coins for every subsequent lap cleared.

Title: Lykrast's website - Where to use the Turbo Dice?
URL: https://lykrast.com/blog/where-to-use-the-turbo-dice
Published: N/A
Author: N/A
Highlights:
Roll 'em Raceway is one of the boards in Jamboree, which is themed after a race track. It has an exclusive item (today's subject): the Turbo Dice. It lets you roll 4 dices at once but you skip any board event you pass through. This mean no collecting the star, no purchasing at the shop, and so on (things that you would have been able to do if you used a Triple Dice instead).

So it's a pretty clear high risk high reward item: it gives you the highest mobility boost of any (non-teleporting) item in the game, but you can't use it to snag stars and stuff, only to reposition. As it has a similar price to the Triple Dice in Jamboree (10 coins for Triple, 12 for Turbo), when is that extra d10 worth the risk of skipping stuff?
...
While I'm at it I'll also include the chance to not skip the event 2 ahead (so for example one the starting line it's the chance to land before the star spawn). Using anydice.com with output 4d10 (and merging the 2 stars because their distance to Boo is the same) we get ... following table:

| Right after | Chance to not skip | | Chance to not skip second | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Finish line | 0.70% | | 59.95% (top) | 46.65% (bottom) |
| Pit Stop | 9.97% | | 90.03% (top) | 82.40% (bottom) |
| Shop | 9.97% (top) | 4.95% (bottom) | 72.20% (passing top) | 59.95% (passing bottom) |
| Star | 2.10% | | 72.20% (finish) | 59.95% (pit stop) |
| Boo | 9.97% (finish) | 4.95% (pit stop) | 59.95% (passing finish) | 82.40% (passing pit) |
...
- Right after the Pit Stop (that may give you a Turbo Dice), skipping the shop and either hoping not to skip the star, or beelining for boo.
- Right after the shop, crossing fingers to not skip Boo; or if you don't have enough money trying to rush the finish line from there (tho boo also gives you money).
- Right after boo, skipping the finish line and pit stop (like if you have enough items and coins? but boo is happy to dump your coins), maybe skipping the shop (but also the pit stop would have given you items), and going straight to the star.
- Don't think it's worth it right before the star, because Boo is both giving you coins (to spend on items at the pit stop or shop) or giving you a way to dump coins (that you get from the board or the finish line).

That does sound like something to consider... but also all events you pass are either opportunities to get more coins (boo, finish line), or turn excess coins into win conditions directly (star, boo star steal), or indirectly (getting mobility from shop or pit stop).
